title: Bounded compactified site comparison commutes with open restriction
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $f:X\to S$ have a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}S$ between Noetherian schemes, where $j$ is open and $r$ is proper [def-weil-compactifications-refinements, def-pc-scheme]. Work in the bounded-below ordinary derived categories of $A$-module sheaves on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $R f_!^{\mathrm{et}}=Rr_*^{\mathrm{et}}Dj_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ be the candidate of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $R f_!^{\mathrm{pro},c}=Rr_*^{\mathrm{pro}}Dj_!^{\mathrm{pro}}$ the corresponding chosen-compactification expression [def-weil-extension-by-zero, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the composite of the canonical open-extension and proper direct-image site comparisons is an isomorphism
$$J_{c,L}:\nu_S^*R f_!^{\mathrm{et}}L\xrightarrow{\sim}R f_!^{\mathrm{pro},c}\nu_X^*L.$$
For every open $u:U\hookrightarrow S$, put $X_U=X\times_SU$, $v:X_U\hookrightarrow X$, and let $c_U$ be the restricted compactification. Let $C^{\mathrm{et}}:u^*Rr_*^{\mathrm{et}}Dj_!^{\mathrm{et}}\to Rr_{U*}^{\mathrm{et}}Dj_{U!}^{\mathrm{et}}v^*$ be the canonical compactified open-restriction exchange: the proper exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] for the cartesian square of $r$ over $u$, followed by $Rr_{U*}$ of the inverse of the open-extension comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. Let $C^{\mathrm{pro}}$ be the composite given by the same two mate constructions [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] on the pro-etale sites. The actual comparison maps satisfy
$$C^{\mathrm{pro}}\circ u_{\mathrm{pro}}^*J_{c,L}=J_{c_U,v^*L}\circ\nu_U^*C^{\mathrm{et}},$$
under the canonical inverse-image comparisons. This equation is natural in $L$ and holds with the canonical direct-image counits and extension-by-zero evaluation counits. It makes no comparison assertion for arbitrary unbounded pro-etale inputs.

proof.text: Put $\overline X_U=\overline X\times_SU$ and write $w:\overline X_U\hookrightarrow\overline X$ for its open inclusion. The two squares are $(r,r_U,u,w)$ and $(j,j_U,w,v)$. Properness implies that $r$ is of finite type, hence quasi-compact; separatedness implies quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The base-change permanence in [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], clause (3), gives the same two properties for $r_U$. Thus both direct-image comparisons used below satisfy the qcqs hypotheses. In the rest of the proof subscripts $e,p$ denote the etale and pro-etale functors, $N_T=\nu_T^*$, and all compositions are read from right to left. Canonical inverse-image identifications are those of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]; its composition and cartesian compatibility allow us to suppress them in equations.

source.place: Tag 09A6, lemma-morphism-comparison: qcqs hypothesis; preceding commutative square of inverse images

proof.text: Let $e=Dj_{e,!}$, $d=Dj_{p,!}$, and similarly $e',d'$ for $j_U$. These functors are termwise exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact, lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. The comparison $N_T$ is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], and etale inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $M=eL$, $v_e^*L$, $w_e^*M$, $N_XL$ and their open extensions remain bounded below. Use precisely the derived open comparison $k_L:N_{\overline X}eL\xrightarrow{\sim}dN_XL$ specified in [lem-fix-site-open-exchange], not an arbitrary isomorphism. That statement identifies $k^{-1}$ with the open-adjunction adjunct of the etale unit followed by the canonical restriction comparison; it therefore fixes the adjunction normalization. Write $k'$ for the same comparison for $j_U$.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison: comparison by the common right adjoint; exact derived extension

proof.text:
For $h=r,r_U$, let $b_h:N Rh_{e,*}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_{p,*}N$ be the specified comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. This node applies by Step 1 and to bounded-below inputs by Step 2; it proves invertibility of this actual counit mate and naturality in its input. The composite in the question is therefore
$$J_{c,L}=Rr_{p,*}(k_L)\circ b_{r,eL}.$$
Each factor is invertible, so $J_{c,L}$ is invertible, naturally in $L$. The same formula with primes gives $J_{c_U,v_e^*L}$. These are the compactification expressions of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and the statement, so no compactification-independence theorem is needed.

source.place: Tag 09A6, lemma-morphism-comparison: named canonical direct-image map; Tag 09AF: open comparison; their composite

proof.text:
Denote the direct-image exchanges for $(r,r_U,u,w)$ by $E^e$ and $E^p$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] with $(f,f',g,g')=(r,r_U,u,w)$ and input $M=eL$. Its equation, under the specified inverse-image comparisons, is
$$E^p_{N_{\overline X}M}\circ u_p^*(b_{r,M})
=b_{r_U,w_e^*M}\circ N_U(E^e_M).\tag{1}$$
All coefficients here are constant $A$-module coefficients. The $E^e$ in this citation is the unit--square--counit mate, exactly as in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]; the $E^p$ is the corresponding ambient ringed mate. Thus (1) concerns the exchanges in the question, including their counits. It does not assume either exchange to be invertible.

source.place: Tag 09A6, lemma-morphism-comparison and the preceding inverse-image square; agent application of the canonical exchange-transport equation

proof.text:
Let $t^e:w_e^*e\xrightarrow{\sim}e'v_e^*$ and $t^p:w_p^*d\xrightarrow{\sim}d'v_p^*$ be the open base-change maps. The direction is important: these are inverses of the extension maps defined in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map], as the unit-adjunct formula of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] shows. Apply [lem-fix-site-open-exchange] to $(j,j_U,w,v)$, with its $\rho$ the inverse pullback comparison. Its full equation, after the canonical inverse-image identifications, reads
$$t^p_{N_XL}\circ w_p^*(k_L)
=k'_{v_e^*L}\circ N_{\overline X_U}(t^e_L).\tag{2}$$
This is an equality of the specified derived maps, natural in $L$, and uses no conservativity or detection of equality by geometric stalks.

source.place: Tag 03S6, lemma-shriek-base-change: comparison of right adjoints and inverse mate direction; Tag 09AF for the normalized site transport

proof.text:
For brevity write $F=Rr_{p,*}$, $F'=Rr_{U,p,*}$, $G'=Rr_{U,e,*}$ and $N'=N_{\overline X_U}$. Keep $M=eL$. By definition the exchanges of the question are $C^p=F'(t^p)\circ E^p_d$ and $C^e=G'(t^e)\circ E^e_e$. Expand the left side of the desired equation. Naturality of $E^p$ in the morphism $k_L$, equation (2), equation (1), and then naturality of $b_{r_U}$ in $t^e_L$ give, in that order,
$$\begin{aligned}
C^p_{N_XL}\circ u_p^*J_{c,L}
&=F'(t^p_{N_XL})\circ E^p_{dN_XL}\circ u_p^*F(k_L)\circ u_p^*b_{r,M}\\
&=F'(t^p_{N_XL}\circ w_p^*k_L)\circ E^p_{N_{\overline X}M}\circ u_p^*b_{r,M}\\
&=F'(k'_{v_e^*L})\circ F'N'(t^e_L)\circ b_{r_U,w_e^*M}\circ N_U(E^e_M)\\
&=F'(k'_{v_e^*L})\circ b_{r_U,e'v_e^*L}\circ N_U(G'(t^e_L))\circ N_U(E^e_M)\\
&=J_{c_U,v_e^*L}\circ N_U(C^e_L).
\end{aligned}$$
Each equality is functoriality or substitution of the two cited transport equations. The suppressed pullback comparisons compose to the ones in the question by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback].

proof.text:
Finally check the normalization clause. For a qcqs $h$, [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] gives
$$\varepsilon^p_h\circ h_p^*(b_h)\circ a_h=N(\varepsilon^e_h),$$
where $a_h:Nh_e^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_p^*N$ is the canonical comparison. For $j$, put $s=j_p^*$, $q=j_e^*$ and $a=N_Xq\xrightarrow{\sim}sN_{\overline X}$. The adjunct formula for $k^{-1}$ in [lem-fix-site-open-exchange] says $s(k^{-1})\eta^p=a_eN_X(\eta^e)$. Consequently the adjunct of $N_{\overline X}(\varepsilon^e_B)\circ k^{-1}_{qB}$ is
$$sN_{\overline X}(\varepsilon^e_B)\circ a_{eqB}\circ N_X(\eta^e_{qB})
=a_B\circ N_X(q\varepsilon^e_B\circ\eta^e_{qB})=a_B.$$
Here the first equality is naturality of $a$ and the second is the etale triangle identity. The adjunct of $\varepsilon^p_{N_{\overline X}B}\circ d(a_B)$ is also $a_B$. The adjunction bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] therefore gives
$$N_{\overline X}(\varepsilon^e_B)
=\varepsilon^p_{N_{\overline X}B}\circ d(a_B)\circ k_{qB}.$$
Thus the $k$ used throughout preserves the actual extension-by-zero evaluation counit. The same holds for $j_U$. All transformations and the computations are natural in $L$; no choices of isomorphisms or changes of adjunction are involved. This proves the remaining normalization and naturality clauses.
